# Collation-aware index key size — facts

> Source-anchored units about Collation-aware index key size: 11 across 4 sources. Each line ends in the URL and anchor it came from; `keywords:` names the lexicon terms that matched.

<!-- generated by llms-concept-abstractor v1.4.1 · generated 2026-10-31 · 11 units · 4 sources · rights: quote -->

## How it works

- [statement] MongoDB warns that collation-aware index keys might be larger than keys without collation because it uses ICU collation keys; ICU describes these as preprocessed byte sequences that preserve the configured comparison order. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/collation.md · keywords: Collation-aware index key size · also: https://unicode-org.github.io/icu/userguide/collation/architecture.html, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/data-modeling/schema-design-process/create-indexes.md

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] For an indexed string comparison, the operation must use the same collation as the index; an operation with a different collation cannot use that index to support the string comparison. A larger collated index is therefore not automatically useful to queries using different string semantics. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/collation.md · keywords: Collation-aware index key size · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/data-modeling/schema-design-process/create-indexes.md

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] For collated MongoDB string values, the index stores ICU binary comparison encodings rather than raw strings; comparing the encodings preserves the language-specific ordering. (high confidence) — https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-60298 · keywords: Collation-aware index key size · also: https://unicode-org.github.io/icu/userguide/collation/architecture.html
- [statement] Methodological inference: compare binary and collated versions of the same compound key pattern on representative text using the intended locale and strength, and measure the resulting index footprint and query behavior rather than applying a blanket expansion percentage. ICU documents variable key sizes, MongoDB recommends analyzing index effectiveness, and PostgreSQL design analysis explains that larger normalized keys can reduce B-tree fan-in. The PostgreSQL discussion is architectural context, not a MongoDB benchmark. (medium confidence) — https://unicode-org.github.io/icu/userguide/collation/architecture.html · keywords: Collation-aware index key size · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/data-modeling/schema-design-process/create-indexes.md, https://wiki.postgresql.org/wiki/Key_normalization
- [statement] Methodological inference: measure representative data under the intended locale and collation settings rather than applying a fixed expansion factor. ICU documents variable key sizes, and the PostgreSQL design discussion explicitly calls for measuring storage costs against benefits. (medium confidence) — https://unicode-org.github.io/icu/userguide/collation/architecture.html · keywords: Collation-aware index key size · also: https://wiki.postgresql.org/wiki/Key_normalization

## Facts and statements

- [statement] ICU sort-key length depends on the alphabet, locale and collation elements, and ICU compresses regular character sequences. A source-string byte count alone therefore does not determine a universal key-size ratio; PostgreSQL key-normalization design discussion independently treats representation growth and compression as workload-dependent tradeoffs. (medium confidence) — https://unicode-org.github.io/icu/userguide/collation/architecture.html · keywords: Collation-aware index key size · also: https://wiki.postgresql.org/wiki/Key_normalization
- [statement] Comparison strength changes which distinctions matter: primary compares base letters, secondary adds accent differences and tertiary adds case differences. ICU encodes comparison levels in sort keys, so sizing should use the exact collation settings required by the application. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/collation.md · keywords: Collation-aware index key size · also: https://unicode-org.github.io/icu/userguide/collation/architecture.html
- [statement] Historical troubleshooting example: SERVER-60298 shows a Spanish-collation equality bound whose internal ICU bytes were exposed as invalid UTF-8 in explain output. Such transformed bounds should not be interpreted as the original string or used to infer its stored key length from the displayed characters. This describes the historical bug, not an assertion that current servers still emit invalid UTF-8. (low confidence) — https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-60298 · keywords: Collation-aware index key size
- [statement] ICU says maximum sort-key size depends on the alphabet and locale and that compression makes regular character sequences compact. Its bytes-per-code-point examples are approximate averages, not safe maximum bounds or MongoDB index-sizing formulas. (low confidence) — https://unicode-org.github.io/icu/userguide/collation/architecture.html · keywords: Collation-aware index key size
- [statement] Collation strength selects comparison levels, and ICU sort keys encode level weights. Higher strengths or an added case level can change storage requirements; reducing strength also changes equality semantics, so size tuning must preserve required comparisons. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/collation.md · keywords: Collation-aware index key size · also: https://unicode-org.github.io/icu/userguide/collation/architecture.html
- [statement] The PostgreSQL key-normalization draft explains that larger normalized keys can reduce B-tree fan-in, while compression and truncation can offset storage overhead. This is architectural context, not a description of MongoDB's index representation. (low confidence) — https://wiki.postgresql.org/wiki/Key_normalization · keywords: Collation-aware index key size
